Bill.BriefDescription: Limiting passengers from riding on the outside part of vehicles.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to passengers riding on the outside part ofvehicles; amending RCW 46.61.660; creating a new section; andprescribing penalties.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) The legislature finds and declares that: (a) Pickup trucks are becoming increasingly popular as multipurposevehicles and are frequently used for family transport and recreation; (b) Each year, a significant number of injuries and deaths occur inthis state as a result of persons riding in the cargo area of pickuptrucks without the use of appropriate restraint devices when doing so; (c) Injuries sustained by persons riding in the cargo area ofpickup trucks without the use of appropriate restraint devices whendoing so occur as a result both of collisions in which the pickuptrucks are involved and of ejections from the pickup trucks duringsudden stops, bumps, turns, or swerves where no collision occurs; and (d) The occupant death rate is higher in pickup trucks and smallutility vehicles than in any other kind of passenger vehicle. (2) It is therefore the purpose of this act to prohibit riding inopen truck beds except in specified circumstances.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 46.61.660 and 1997 c 190 s 1 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) It ((shall be unlawful)) is a traffic infraction for any personto transport any living animal on the running board, fenders, hood, orother outside part of any vehicle unless suitable harness, cage orenclosure be provided and so attached as to protect such animal fromfalling or being thrown therefrom. (2) It ((shall be unlawful)) is a traffic infraction for any personto transport any persons upon the running board, fenders, hood or otheroutside part of any vehicle, except that this provision shall not applyto authorized emergency vehicles or to solid waste collection vehiclesthat are engaged in collecting solid waste or recyclables on route atspeeds of twenty miles per hour or less. (3)(a) It is a traffic infraction for any person to transport anypersons in or on an open truck bed. This subsection does not apply toa person operating: (i) An authorized emergency vehicle; (ii) A vehicle where the passengers are wearing safety belts in aproperly adjusted and securely fastened manner; (iii) A vehicle in a parade, caravan, or exhibition that isofficially authorized or otherwise permitted by law; or (iv) A vehicle while performing those practices that are prudentand necessary for the purpose of producing agricultural goods and theharvesting of natural resources. (b) For the purposes of this subsection, "open truck bed" includesa pickup truck bed without a shell or camper, whether a tailgate is upor down, and the bed of a flatbed truck.
